name: Cysteamine

lead: Cysteamine is an aminothiol drug approved for treating nephropathic cystinosis, and a topical cream is also used for melasma and hyperpigmentation. Its dermatologic use is positioned as a non-hydroquinone depigmenting option.
Controlled studies in melasma have shown improvement compared with vehicle, though trials are modest in size.

paras: In skin, cysteamine is thought to inhibit tyrosinase and peroxidase, scavenge free radicals and chelate iron and copper, reducing melanin formation.

The main drawbacks are a strong sulfurous odor, stinging and redness, and the instability of the molecule in water. Systemic cysteamine drugs have additional gastrointestinal and other side effects, and its availability as a cosmetic versus a medicine varies by country.
